definitions.explanation: The pursuit of or devotion to beauty and sensuous pleasure, especially in art and literature. In modern Japanese pop culture, also refers to a genre featuring beautiful, often romantic depictions of male characters.

examples.japanese: {耽美|たんび}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧な⟦{世界観|せかいかん}→世界観：11312_sekaikan⟧。

{耽美|たんび}⟦{主義|しゅぎ}→主義：03215_shugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{文学|ぶんがく}→文学：01505_bungaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{美|うつく}しさ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{重要|じゅうよう}→重要：01575_juuyou⟧な⟦{価値|かち}→価値：00131_kachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Aestheticist literature regards beauty as the most important value.

examples.japanese: {谷崎|たにざき}{潤一郎|じゅんいちろう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{耽美|たんび}⟦{派|は}→派：28356_ha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{作家|さっか}→作家：01414_sakka⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: Tanizaki Jun'ichiro is known as a leading writer of the Japanese aestheticist school.

notes: In literary criticism, {耽美|たんび}⟦{主義|しゅぎ}→主義：03215_shugi⟧ (aestheticism) refers to the art-for-art's-sake movement. Japanese writers associated with this school include {谷崎|たにざき}{潤一郎|じゅんいちろう} and {永井|ながい}{荷風|かふう}. In modern pop culture, {耽美|たんび} is used as a genre label for manga, anime, and fiction featuring idealized, often androgynous male characters and romantic relationships between men (overlapping with BL/⟦ボーイズラブ→ボーイズラブ：26336_booizurabu⟧). Common compounds: {耽美|たんび}⟦{主義|しゅぎ}→主義：03215_shugi⟧ (aestheticism), {耽美|たんび}⟦{的|てき}→〜的：09839_teki⟧ (aesthetic), {耽美|たんび}⟦{派|は}→派：28356_ha⟧ (aestheticist school).
